purpose: Chlorthalidone is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of heart attack and stroke. It is also used to reduce swelling caused by excess fluid buildup in your body, known as edema. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and blood vessels over time.
how_it_works: This medication works by telling your kidneys to remove extra salt and water from your body through your urine. Because there is less fluid in your blood vessels, your blood pressure goes down. Think of it like releasing pressure from a garden hose by letting some water out.
common_side_effects: You may urinate more often, especially when you first start taking it. Other common effects include feeling dizzy or lightheaded when you stand up, muscle cramps, feeling thirsty, low potassium levels, and sensitivity to sunlight. Most of these tend to improve as your body adjusts.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have signs of low potassium such as muscle weakness, cramps, or irregular heartbeat. Avoid getting dehydrated — drink enough fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Let your doctor know if you have diabetes, kidney disease, gout, or are allergic to sulfa drugs. Do not stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 12.5 to 25 mg taken by mouth once daily in the morning. Your doctor may adjust it up to 50 mg per day depending on how you respond. Taking it in the morning helps prevent the need to urinate at night.
